narration.text: [softly] Look at this lake. Calm. Blue. [short pause] In one night, it breathed out. [long pause] Cameroon, August, nineteen eighty six. Villages sleep in the valleys below Lake Nyos. [long pause] Late at night, people hear a deep rumble. Some see a white mist rise from the water. [long pause] The mist is carbon dioxide, heavier than air. It pours over the rim and down the valleys, like water. [long pause] [whispers] By morning, the valleys are silent. [long pause] [softly] One thousand, seven hundred and forty six people died that night. Many in their homes. [long pause] For years, gas from deep below had gathered at the bottom of the lake, held down by the weight of the water. [long pause] That night, something disturbed it. Scientists still debate what. [long pause] Today, pipes draw the gas up from the bottom, so it cannot build up like that again. [long pause] [whispers] But other lakes on Earth are still holding their breath.
